title: Choose the visual world for Giannia's portfolio
question: Every work is a sticker; the notebook is what holds them. Keep the assigned world, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Trace Roll
options.lineage: the roll of canary trace on an architecture student's light table
options.thesis: Her notebook is a sketchbook of yellow trace on a light table: works are stickers pressed onto layered sheets, and filtering slides a sheet of trace over the ones that don't match.
options.viewport: A trace-paper sketchbook spread on a glowing light table; a dozen die-cut work stickers on the top sheet, pencil leader lines run from each to a handwritten note; filters sit along the spine as pencil tabs.
options.risk: Pale yellow on white can wash out; stickers and type must carry full contrast or the page reads faint.

raised.raise: Every note is pinned to its sticker by a pencil leader line, the way a drawing annotates a node; nothing floats.
State is depth: matching works sit on the top sheet, filtered-out works sink under one more sheet of trace, one rule for every state.
One loud entry point: the featured work's sticker is set at twice the scale of the rest, so the eye enters there.
Every detail page walks the same stations in order: brief, site, drawings, model, reflection.

options.label: The Dot-Grid Sketchbook
options.lineage: the dot-grid sketchbook every studio carries
options.thesis: An open dot-grid sketchbook spread, works as white-bordered die-cut stickers with washi tape, handwritten captions in the margins.
options.viewport: Two notebook pages on a gutter, stickers scattered across both, her name handwritten at top left, filters as tabbed page edges.
options.risk: The literal reading of the brief and the place most runs land: warm, legible, but close to every scrapbook template.

options.label: Cut-Paper Wit
options.thesis: Each work is a cut-paper sticker whose shape is a visual pun on the building, set on a white sheet with crayon overshoots.
options.viewport: Her name scrawled in marker, works as cut-paper silhouettes of each project, a crayon ring around the one under the cursor.
options.case: Cutest of the hand and the image is the label, which suits stickers; loses on audience identification because it reads as graphic design rather than architecture.
options.risk: Can tip into children's-book whimsy and undersell serious drawings.

options.label: Glazed Partition
options.thesis: The catalog is a glazed wall elevation: each work a pane, hover backlights it, the selected category floods its panes with colour.
options.viewport: A wall of panes in a black steel grid, her name etched in one pane, works as stickers on the glass.
options.case: Most architecture-native and very clear to scan; loses the diary and the cute, which the brief asks for.
options.risk: Professional but cold; the notebook warmth disappears.

options.label: Ray Gun Layout Desk
options.thesis: Colliding type and overprinted photos, the page felt before it is read.
options.viewport: Overlapping headlines with project photos printed through them.
options.case: Fights the professional reviewer who needs to scan in a minute.
options.kept: One loud entry point per page: the featured sticker at double scale.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: A force network where every element is held by its counterforce.
options.viewport: A strut network with annotations on leader lines.
options.case: An engineering diagram, not a diary; no warmth.
options.risk: Cold and abstract for a personal portfolio.
options.kept: Annotations pinned to their subject on leader lines.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Rank is depth over a black void.
options.viewport: One line of bitmap text over drifting particles.
options.case: No link to architecture or a notebook.
options.risk: Reads as a game, not a portfolio.
options.kept: State is depth: one consistent rule maps every state to a layer.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Images emerge through fixed stations under amber light.
options.viewport: Prints in trays under amber light.
options.case: Atmospheric but drowns drawings in amber.
options.kept: Fixed stations in order: every project told in the same sequence.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The architecture-student portfolio as it usually ships: white page, name top left, a clean grid of project thumbnails.
canonCard.viewport: Name and three links across the top, a 3-column grid of project images with captions.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other applicant's portfolio, and no stickers or notebook at all.
